item.title: Laws X, 890b–891c: Why do the interlocutors find it important to argue at length that gods exist and are good?
item.description: Obviously, it is in response to the atheists, and thus serves an apologetic purpose. But the interlocutors say more than that. Consider also remarks at 886e–887c and 887e–888d. We have already partly answered this question, so we can begin by reviewing the relevant bits from other answers.

item.description: Thanks to the commenters. We've really had only six people offering substantive comments on the answers.
